relation_coverage.$comment: WHICH PAIRS the distance and angular edges are actually emitted for. This is the single most common source of a spec that compiles, passes its hand-written scenarios, and can never fire on a capture.

proximity_and_angular_pairs.rule: Emitted only for ordered pairs matching DEFAULT_PROXIMITY_RELATIONS / DEFAULT_DIRECTIONAL_RELATIONS, every entry of which pairs the base class `ego` with one other base class.
proximity_and_angular_pairs.ego_is_always_one_end: There is NEVER a proximity or angular edge between two non-ego actors. Any two non-ego actors are therefore unrelated by distance and by angle, and a schema binding such a pair grounds while nothing it asks about can ever hold.

excluded_and_why.van: not listed in DEFAULT_PROXIMITY_RELATIONS at all
excluded_and_why.traffic_light: the table spells it `traffic light` (space) while the base class is `traffic_light` (underscore), so the equality test never matches
excluded_and_why.stop_sign: the table spells it `stop sign` while the base class is `stop_sign`
excluded_and_why.junction_boundary: not listed; a boundary node exists only when the map was parsed with parse_junction_boundaries, and even then no distance edge reaches it

proximity_and_angular_pairs.consequence: No distance to any sign or signal exists. Use `controls` / `mayAffect`. And a rule about an emergency vehicle plus a distance can only ground on the police car (`car`) and the firetruck (`truck`), never the ambulance (`van`).
proximity_and_angular_pairs.lean_binders: Core/Grounding.lean's proximityVehicleBinder / proximityRoadUserBinder range over exactly the covered classes; roadUserBinder and vehicleBinder do not, and admit types that carry no proximity edge. The binder definitions are in Core and are not repeated here — what is here is the coverage rule they exist to respect.
proximity_and_angular_pairs.static_background_vehicles: The covered base classes include entities that are NOT actors. sgg.py Step 4 (:412-466) ingests the map's parked-vehicle level geometry via `world.get_environment_objects(CityObjectLabel.Car/Bus/Truck/Bicycle/Motorcycle)` (or the single `Vehicles` label on older CARLA, :424-426) with the enum string as `sem_class` (:456), and `actors.py::base_type_map` maps those strings to the real base classes ('Car'->'car', 'Vehicles'->'vehicle', ...) — every one of which except `vehicle` is in the proximity table. So parked scenery becomes a `.car` carrying the same proximity and angular edges as moving traffic, with the same EntityType, the same bands and the same empty `special_class`. The two marks the generator leaves: the scenery branch reaches __add_to_graph with `entity_id=-static_id` (:462) and never runs the actor loop's `carla_id`/`carla_type_id` writes (:681-682), so `carla_id` is ABSENT and `entity_id` negative (older generator versions passed no entity_id at all); and `sem_class` is the capitalised enum name rather than a `vehicle.*` blueprint id. carla/adapter.py lifts either mark as the boolean `map_scenery`, read by Pred.isMapScenery, and keys the entity's identity on its fixed position. Consequence: any binder over a vehicle type grounds on scenery, so a distance test with no lane test attached can hold against a static map object rather than a road user; a rule about another vehicle's CONDUCT should exclude it with Pred.isMapScenery, and a rule about a standing obstruction may want exactly it.

inter_lane_edges.rule: `opposes`, `toLeftOf` and `toRightOf` between lane nodes are emitted only for ADJACENT lane ids of the same road (`zip(sorted_lanes, sorted_lanes[1:])`).
inter_lane_edges.consequence: Two lanes separated by a third carry none of these labels, and lanes of different roads are never related this way.

governance_edges.$comment: Which edges carry GOVERNANCE — the fact that a signal or sign applies to a vehicle. Only `controls` and `mayAffect` do. Both are built from a geometric test, and the two signal kinds do not use the same one, which is the single most consequential asymmetry in this data model.
governance_edges.built_from: Both are drawn from a signal or sign to DRIVING NODES, never to a vehicle. A vehicle is associated with a signal transitively: the vehicle is `isIn` a lane and the signal `controls` that lane.
governance_edges.traffic_light_targets: A traffic light's `controls` edges come from `TrafficLight.get_affected_lane_waypoints()`, matched to a driving node within `segment_length * 0.5` in three dimensions (sgg.py:628-631, plane_projection=False). CARLA's API documents that method as returning "the positions and lanes where the traffic light is having an effect", and documents a SEPARATE method, `get_stop_waypoints()`, as returning "the stop position for the traffic light ... where a vehicle should stop". The generator calls the first and never the second. So a light's `controls` edge marks the lanes the signal acts ON, not the place a driver is required to stop, and the approach-side stop position is absent from the graph entirely. On a CARLA build lacking `get_affected_lane_waypoints` the fallback (:632-635) intersects the light's `trigger_volume` with the driving nodes instead — the stop sign's construction — so on such a capture the two device kinds are built alike.
governance_edges.stop_sign_targets: A stop sign's `controls` edges come from the sign's `trigger_volume`, intersected against driving nodes. A trigger volume is the region in which the sign takes effect on an approaching vehicle, so this edge and the traffic light's are built from different geometry despite sharing one relation label. A rule that reads `controls` uniformly across both signal kinds is reading two different things.
governance_edges.consequence_for_a_formula: Requiring a light's `controls` governance AND the vehicle being outside the intersection may be unsatisfiable on generator output, because the two conditions are built from different geometry. An unsatisfiable antecedent is never a false positive — it is silently always-compliant, and it still grounds, so the vacuity guard does not catch it either. Read the grounding count the gate reports rather than predicting satisfiability.
governance_edges.landmarks: `mayAffect` links an OpenDRIVE landmark to every driving node whose `Waypoint.get_landmarks(render_dist)` returned it (sgg.py:695-698) — the landmarks AHEAD of that waypoint along its own lane, within render distance — provided the landmark itself lies inside the ego's render box (:699). The edge is therefore directional along the road but blind to which carriageway the sign faces: on a two-way road it reaches lanes of both directions. Two lifted attributes state the governance the edge only approximates: `landmark_orientation`, which says which direction of travel the sign faces in the same terms the lane-id sign is written in (Pred.landmarkFacesLane / landmarkOrientedFor), and `landmark_lane_validities`, the lane range the map declares it valid for (Pred.landmarkValidForLane / landmarkGoverns). Maps frequently populate the first and leave the second empty.
governance_edges.recovering_the_approach_association: The approach-side association is NOT lost, only indirect. The lane a driver waits in leads into the lane the signal acts on, and the generator records that as `travelsTo`, so the connection exists in the data. No predicate currently walks it: `Pred.governs` reads the `controls` edge directly and therefore holds only once a vehicle is already in the controlled lane. Expressing governance from the approach is a VOCABULARY GAP — name it in the plan — not a data gap, and not grounds for recording a law unsupported. How many `travelsTo` hops such a predicate should walk is not something the data settles: a lane node exists per (junction, road, lane) triple, so an approach spanning several roads spans several nodes, and any fixed depth is a modelling choice rather than a generator fact.
governance_edges.what_is_still_absent: A stop-line POSITION. CARLA computes stop waypoints from a light's trigger boxes and exposes them as a separate call the generator never makes, so no node or edge marks where a vehicle is required to halt. Lane nodes carry no coordinates either, so the distance to a stop line is not expressible. The signal HEAD does carry a position (lifted as pos_x/pos_y/pos_z), so a metric separation from the signal itself is the nearest available substitute — a different quantity, and one to state as a residue rather than pass off as the stop line. Emitting the stop association as its own edge is a generator extension, not missing data.

isIn_edges.$comment: WHICH PAIRS `isIn` relates. It is overloaded across three levels.
isIn_edges.levels: entity→lane, lane→road, road→junction all use `isIn`. Query it type-filtered (`Scene.relatedToTyped`, or the typed predicates in Core/Vocab.lean); an unfiltered query mixes the three.
isIn_edges.from_a_sign_is_not_governance: Every actor gets `isIn` edges to the driving nodes its bounding box overlaps (sgg.py::__add_to_graph), signs included, so a sign's `isIn` matches the sign facing the cross street just as well. Use `controls` or `mayAffect` for governance.
isIn_edges.off_road_is_also_out_of_reach: The `Off Road` node collects every actor with no edge to a driving node the abstraction KEPT (sgg_abstractor.py:247-248), and the driving nodes it keeps are those within the road-grade tolerance of the ego's own height (:131-132, utils.py::valid_gradient). A vehicle on an overpass or underpass relative to the ego, a sign whose bounding box overlaps no lane, and a landmark — placed by its transform, with no box — are all `isIn Off Road` while standing on or beside a perfectly good road. `Pred.offRoadway` therefore means 'over no kept driving lane', not 'off the carriageway'.

attribute_keys.$comment: What a rule can read. The KEY LIST is not here: it is derived from carla/adapter.py's mapping tables and Core/Builders.lean, the two things that actually put an attribute on an entity, so it cannot drift from them. What is here is what only this file knows — for each key, its kind, which entities carry it, its unit, and the generator attribute it was lifted from. `from_generator_key` is the only record of the rename.

name.source: The RSV node name. NOT the entity identity: carla/adapter.py assigns a Lean EntityId per physical entity, resolved from `carla_id`, the ego's own `entity_id`, a landmark's `landmark_id`, or for a static node its fixed position, and only structure nodes are keyed by name, which for them IS the OpenDRIVE identity. The generator composes actor names as the base class followed by a PER-FRAME counter over the actors present (sgg_abstractor.py:234-235), so the same name denotes different vehicles in different frames as actors enter and leave the render box; a rule that reads `name` on an actor reads that counter.

sem_class.on: actors, signals, signs and landmarks; on a lane node it is the builder constant "Driving" (the RSV lane node carries no attributes, Core/Builders.lean::mkLane writes it), and roads, junctions and Off Road carry none
sem_class.source: the CARLA blueprint / type id the generator copies into Node.attr

base_class.source: NOT an entry in the RSV node's attribute dict. The RSV `Node` is `(name, base_class, attr)`, so base_class is a field on the node OBJECT, set from `actors.py::get_base_type`; the attr dict the abstraction copies never contains it. carla/adapter.py reads the field to choose the Lean EntityType, and Core/Builders.lean re-derives the attribute from that type via EntityType.baseClass. So it IS readable, with one exception: the ego builder hard-codes base_class to "ego" rather than to its vehicle class, so a base-class test written to mean 'is a vehicle of this kind' excludes the ego. Use the type predicates instead.

special_class.source: actors.py::get_special_type; empty string when ordinary. Prefer Pred.isEgo / isEmergency

accel.source: the magnitude of the graph's own `carla_acc_x/y/z` components (carla/adapter.py::ego_accel), which is a computation on this frame's data; ego_logs state.acceleration.value only when the components are absent

at_traffic_light.source: carla_affected_by_traffic_light (ego.is_at_traffic_light()) — inside a governing signal's trigger volume, says nothing about its colour

light_state.source: sgg.py:639 writes `light_state = str(actor.state)` on each traffic-light node every frame; values are `carla.TrafficLightState.names` (Red / Yellow / Green / Off / Unknown).

road_id.source: re-read from the node name by Core/Builders.lean

lane_id.source: re-read from the node name; sign is the OpenDRIVE side of the road reference line, negative right / positive left, and all lanes of one travel direction share a sign

posted_limit_kph.source: the trailing number of the blueprint id traffic.speed_limit.<kph>

landmark_type.meaning: Sign-catalogue code, from `landmark.type` (sgg.py:705). Meaningful only within the catalogue named by `landmark_country`: the same code denotes different signs in different catalogues, so a rule that reads one must pin the country too. Not a value — the magnitude is `landmark_value` and its unit is `landmark_unit`.

pos_x.source: `vertex` component x, written for every actor and static node by sgg.py:798 __add_to_graph. Structure nodes (lane, road, junction, offRoad) are built with no attr dict at all (sgg_abstractor.py:145,147,152,222) and so carry no position.

pos_y.source: `vertex` component y, written for every actor and static node by sgg.py:798 __add_to_graph. Structure nodes (lane, road, junction, offRoad) are built with no attr dict at all (sgg_abstractor.py:145,147,152,222) and so carry no position.

fwd_x.source: `forward` component x, sgg.py:798 __add_to_graph. Gives an actor's absolute heading. A LANE has no direction vector, so this cannot be compared against the lane occupied — a lane node carries no attributes at all. One generator path writes `forward` wrongly: the traffic-light branch that iterates `get_light_boxes()` stores `bbox.location + <unit forward>` (:595-600), a POINT one metre ahead of the lamp head, where the fallback branch (:618) stores the direction. carla/adapter.py::heading_vector recovers the direction by subtracting `vertex` whenever the raw value cannot be a unit vector, so `fwd_*` is a heading on every node type.

fwd_y.source: `forward` component y, sgg.py:798 __add_to_graph. Gives an actor's absolute heading. A LANE has no direction vector, so this cannot be compared against the lane occupied — a lane node carries no attributes at all. One generator path writes `forward` wrongly: the traffic-light branch that iterates `get_light_boxes()` stores `bbox.location + <unit forward>` (:595-600), a POINT one metre ahead of the lamp head, where the fallback branch (:618) stores the direction. carla/adapter.py::heading_vector recovers the direction by subtracting `vertex` whenever the raw value cannot be a unit vector, so `fwd_*` is a heading on every node type.

gear.source: `carla_gear`, copy_carla_control (sgg.py:859), which sgg.py:562 calls for the ego node alone. Distinct from `reverse`: that is the control input, which can be set while the vehicle still rolls forward. Read with Pred.inReverseGear.

light_interior.source: `light_Interior`, one of the booleans sgg.py:689 writes per member of `carla.VehicleLightState.names` for every `carla.Vehicle`. The cabin light. Special1/Special2 are read together by Pred.beaconOn, and are the only attributes that distinguish a RESPONDING emergency vehicle from one at rest — the blueprint name does not.

light_special_1.source: `light_Special1`, one of the booleans sgg.py:689 writes per member of `carla.VehicleLightState.names` for every `carla.Vehicle`. An emergency beacon. Special1/Special2 are read together by Pred.beaconOn, and are the only attributes that distinguish a RESPONDING emergency vehicle from one at rest — the blueprint name does not.

carla_id.on: every non-ego actor and every traffic-light node — NOT the ego (sgg.py:560-563 write no id on the ego node; its actor id is `entity_id`, :837), not landmarks, not map scenery
carla_id.source: `carla_id`, the CARLA actor id (sgg.py:681, and :607/:623 on the two traffic-light paths). Stable across frames, and since carla/adapter.py keys Lean entity ids on it, what a binding follows from frame to frame. Rendered as a plain integer string, so `attrEq` and `attrMilli*` both read it.

landmark_lane_validities.source: `landmark_lane_validities` (sgg.py:719), the lane range an OpenDRIVE signal is valid for. This is the governance the `mayAffect` edge only approximates: the edge says the landmark was within render distance of a lane, this says which lanes the sign actually governs. Rendered as the raw OpenDRIVE tuple list. Read by Pred.landmarkValidForLane / landmarkGoverns, which narrow `mayAffect` to the lanes the sign actually governs.

landmark_orientation.source: `landmark.orientation` (sgg.py:710), the carla.LandmarkOrientation enum, decoded by carla/adapter.py::landmark_orientation_name. CARLA's API reference defines Positive as facing vehicles travelling in the road's reference direction — the lanes with NEGATIVE OpenDRIVE ids — Negative as facing the positive lanes, and Both as both. Paired with the lane node's `lane_id` by Pred.landmarkFacesLane / landmarkOrientedFor / landmarkOfTypeOrientedFor, which narrow `mayAffect` to the carriageway the sign faces.

landmark_is_dynamic.source: `landmark.is_dynamic` (sgg.py:720): whether the map records the signal as changeable, which is how OpenDRIVE distinguishes a traffic-light head from a static sign. Read by Pred.landmarkIsDynamic.

landmark_id.source: `landmark.id` (sgg.py:717), the OpenDRIVE signal id: the landmark's identity across frames, which carla/adapter.py keys its Lean entity on. The RSV name `landmark_<country>_<type>_<sub>_<n>` ends in a per-frame counter and is not an identity.

map_scenery.on: vehicle-typed entities the level geometry placed, emitted only when true
map_scenery.source: derived by carla/adapter.py::scenery_attrs from the two marks sgg.py Step 4 leaves on a parked prop: a negative `entity_id` (:462) or a `sem_class` that is a CityObjectLabel member name rather than a blueprint id (:456). Read by Pred.isMapScenery; see relation_coverage.proximity_and_angular_pairs.static_background_vehicles.

Absent on a capture whose generator predated the box, and on every structure node. Read by Pred.surfaceGapAtLeastCentimetres / surfaceGapAtMostCentimetres / hasExtent, which bound the gap between two bodies' SURFACES where `pos_*` alone gives only centre to centre.

attribute_keys.decimal_note: Decimal and integer attributes are float- or int-formatted strings of arbitrary precision. Compare them with TrafficSpec.Pred.attrMilli* (milli-unit integer comparison; 1 m/s = 1000, and "-1" is -1000), never by string equality. Booleans are the literal strings "true" / "false"; read them with Pred.attrTrue, and note that an absent boolean reads as false, which is the correct default for a light that is off.
attribute_keys.no_float_ever: There is no Float anywhere in the library. Comparisons stay decidable and kernel-clean.

$comment: How to READ each part of the generator's output: what it gives, the code that produces it, what it cannot express, and which predicates read it.

Keyed by the DATA ELEMENT, never by a statutory concept. The previous keys were concepts — `posted_speed_limit`, `off_the_carriageway`, `another_vehicle_braking_or_signalling` — and a concept-keyed list is selected by whichever laws someone happened to be formalizing. Keyed by the data, the selection is decided by the artifact instead: `covers` names the entity types, relation labels and attribute keys each entry explains, and `run_spec doctor` fails when an element of Core/Scene.lean is neither covered here nor listed in `no_note_needed`.
It does NOT say which construction to use, or how a limit compares with a statute's wording. Both are formalization decisions, and formalizing is the agent's job.

Two structural boundaries account for most true absences, and both are properties of the abstraction rather than of any law. STRUCTURE NODES CARRY NO ATTRIBUTES: the RSV `Node` defaults `attr` to `{}` and every lane, road, junction and off-road node is built without one, so nothing about the road structure has a position, width, marking or direction vector. WAYPOINT DETAIL IS COLLAPSED: the abstraction folds every waypoint of a lane into one such node, so anything the base graph put on a waypoint — `angle`, `curve`, the lane width and both lane markings — is unreachable by any adapter change, and only a different abstraction would recover it.

landmark_nodes_and_mayAffect.available: OpenDRIVE landmarks carrying a catalogue code in `landmark_type`, a magnitude in `landmark_value` and its unit in `landmark_unit`, linked to lanes by `mayAffect`, narrowed to the carriageway they face by `landmark_orientation` and to the governed lanes by `landmark_lane_validities`, marked as signal heads by `landmark_is_dynamic`, and identified across frames by `landmark_id`. The code space is the whole catalogue, not one restriction: priority, prohibition, mandatory direction and dimensional limits are all reached by naming their code, and no vocabulary extension is needed for a sign kind the library has not seen. Separately, `traffic.speed_limit.<kph>` sign actors carry `posted_limit_kph`, whose unit is fixed by the CARLA blueprint id rather than by the map.
landmark_nodes_and_mayAffect.mechanism: carla_sgg/sgg.py:695-698 collects, for each driving node, the landmarks `Waypoint.get_landmarks(render_dist)` returns — those AHEAD of the waypoint along its lane, within render distance — and keeps a landmark only if it also lies inside the ego's render box (:699); :700-724 writes the node and the `mayAffect` edges.
landmark_nodes_and_mayAffect.data_limit: A landmark reaches the graph only within the capture's render distance of a driving node and inside the ego's render box, so its absence does not establish that the road is unrestricted. `mayAffect` is directional along the road but blind to the carriageway: on a two-way road it reaches lanes of both directions, which is what `landmark_orientation` resolves. The sign ACTORS carry no governance edge at all — only bounding-box `isIn`. Neither the catalogue code nor the unit is assumed by the library; a map may also leave `landmark_country`, `landmark_type` or `landmark_sub_type` empty or set to -1, and the node name then reads `landmark__<type>_-1`. A rule supplies the code; a magnitude is comparable only against a bound in the unit the sign itself states, because a code fixes what is restricted but not which dimension the value is in, so no conversion is possible here. Every one of these — no landmark, unknown code, mismatched unit, unreadable value, unset orientation — makes the predicate FALSE, which is the compliant direction, so pair it with Pred.hasSpeedLimitOfType or Pred.landmarkOfTypeApplies where absence and satisfaction must be told apart.
landmark_nodes_and_mayAffect.vocabulary: Pred.landmarkOfTypeApplies / landmarkOfTypeGoverns / landmarkOfTypeOrientedFor / landmarkType / landmarkSubType / landmarkCountry / landmarkUnit / landmarkStatesAtMost / landmarkStatesAtLeast / landmarkValidForLane / landmarkGoverns / landmarkApplies / landmarkOrientation / landmarkFacesLane / landmarkOrientedFor / landmarkIsDynamic, and for speed specifically Pred.withinSpeedLimitOfType / exceedsSpeedLimitOfType / hasSpeedLimitOfType / postedLimitSignAtMostKph

inter_lane_left_right_edges.available: Lane-to-lane `toLeftOf` / `toRightOf`, each computed in the TARGET lane's own forward frame. The edge PATTERN between two lanes therefore reveals their relative direction of travel: asymmetric (`a toLeftOf b` with `b toRightOf a`) means same direction, mutual (`a toLeftOf b` and `b toLeftOf a`) means opposite, because each lane is judged from its own heading.
inter_lane_left_right_edges.mechanism: carla_sgg/sgg_abstractor.py:161 pairs consecutive sorted lane ids; :193-195 chooses the label from the bearing between them.
inter_lane_left_right_edges.data_limit: The only lateral structure is lane adjacency. There is no carriageway, no kerb, no centre line and no lane width, so no node or edge denotes a fraction or half of the roadway. A vehicle occupying no lane at all satisfies no lane predicate.
inter_lane_left_right_edges.vocabulary: Pred.inOutermostLane / hasLaneToTheSide / laneBesideSameDirection, and the left- and right-hand specialisations of each
inter_lane_left_right_edges.do_not_use: The `lane_id` SIGN (Pred.laneRightOfReference / laneLeftOfReference / inLaneRightOfReference / inLaneLeftOfReference). It records which side of the OpenDRIVE reference line a lane was authored on. Every lane of one direction of travel shares the sign, so on a divided road, or a one-way street the map numbers positively, an entire lawful carriageway is `left of reference`. The sign is a property of how the map was drawn, and the abstraction preserves no relation between it and any direction of travel. The ONE sound use of the sign is against a landmark's own `landmark_orientation`, which the map states in exactly these terms — Pred.landmarkFacesLane — because there the two sides of the comparison share a convention.

angular_edges_and_lane_connectivity.available: Angular edges are computed in the TARGET actor's frame: the generator takes the bearing from actor1's `forward` to the displacement actor1 -> actor2, buckets it, and adds `actor2 --sector--> actor1`, so `a inDFrontOf b` places a in b's front sector as judged from b's heading and says nothing about a's own heading. Two actors are mutually `inFrontOf` exactly when their headings differ by more than 90 degrees. Separately, lane connectivity is directed: `l2 travelsTo l1` states the direction of travel between two lane nodes, and an actor's lane membership is observable per frame.
angular_edges_and_lane_connectivity.mechanism: carla_sgg/sgg_abstractor.py:257-310 — the bearing at :272-282, the sector label at :303-310 from DEFAULT_DIRECTIONAL_THRESHOLDS (see capture_preconditions.directional_split_degrees), the actor-to-actor toLeftOf/toRightOf at :296-302; `travelsTo` and `laneChange` at :196-217.
angular_edges_and_lane_connectivity.data_limit: A mutual angular pair is SYMMETRIC: it establishes that two actors converge, not which of them is misplaced. Lane membership changes only when the actor crosses into another lane node, and the dynamics channels are written for the ego node alone (sgg.py:562-563), so the ego is the only actor whose membership is reliably tracked frame to frame. No lane node carries a direction vector, so an actor's absolute heading cannot be compared with its own lane. `laneChange` is a per-LANE permission, not a per-position one: the route planner's lane-change edge is extended to every node of the lane once any segment permits the change (sgg.py:175-176, :259-305), and the marking that permits or forbids it at a given point survives only on the base graph.
angular_edges_and_lane_connectivity.vocabulary: Pred.oncoming / sameHeading / headingAlignedWith / headingOpposedTo / opposingLanes / laneTravelsTo / inLane

junction_membership_and_controls.available: `stopped` (ego speed <= 0.1 m/s), `inAnyJunction` / `inJunction`, `approachingJunctionWithin` (the actor's lane reaches a junction lane in a caller-supplied number of `travelsTo` steps; the graph settles no reach of its own), and `facingStopSign` via the `controls` edge.
junction_membership_and_controls.mechanism: carla_sgg/sgg_abstractor.py:137 groups driving waypoints by their OpenDRIVE `junction_id`, :143-150 hangs each such road under a `Junction` node by `isIn`; an actor's own membership is then its bounding-box overlap with a waypoint box of a lane in that junction (sgg.py:793).
junction_membership_and_controls.data_limit: No stop line, give-way line or junction boundary has a position, because structure nodes carry no attributes at all (sgg_abstractor.py:19-23), so the only positions distinguishable are inside a junction, in a lane that leads to one, and neither. Durations are frame counts; the rate lives at time_base.capture_hz.
junction_membership_and_controls.vocabulary: Pred.stopped / facingStopSign / approachingJunctionWithin / inAnyJunction, plus TrafficSpec.secondsToFrames

vehicle_light_booleans.available: `light_brake`, `light_left_blinker`, `light_right_blinker`, `light_high_beam`, `light_low_beam`, `light_position`, `light_fog`, `light_reverse`, `light_interior`, `light_special_1`, `light_special_2` on every vehicle EXCEPT the ego.
vehicle_light_booleans.mechanism: carla_sgg/sgg.py:689 writes one boolean per member of `carla.VehicleLightState.names` for every `carla.Vehicle` reached by the actor loop. The ego is never in that loop: generate_graph_for_frame appends `self.ego_id` to `exclude_ids` unconditionally (sgg.py:543-544) and the loop filters on `actor.id not in exclude_ids` (:575). Conversely the `carla_*` state and control channels are written for the ego node alone (:562-563), so the two families never appear on the same node.
vehicle_light_booleans.data_limit: A light reports an actuation, not the motion that follows, and it is false whenever nothing actuated it — in simulation that means false unless the Traffic Manager was told to drive vehicle lights. These booleans are the ONLY dynamic evidence the abstraction keeps about a non-ego vehicle. Map scenery (`map_scenery`) carries none of them either, having never passed through the actor loop; Pred.isMapScenery separates it.

off_road_node.available: An actor with no driving-lane edge is `isIn` the single `Off Road` node (`Pred.offRoadway`).
off_road_node.mechanism: carla_sgg/sgg_abstractor.py:248 attaches any such actor to the `Off Road` node.
off_road_node.data_limit: `Sidewalk` nodes are filtered out by process_to_junction_rsv, so pavement, verge and central reservation collapse into that one node and are indistinguishable from each other. The node also collects everything with no edge to a KEPT driving node, and the kept nodes are gradient-filtered against the ego's height (sgg_abstractor.py:131-132): a vehicle on an overpass or underpass relative to the ego, a sign overlapping no lane, and every landmark (placed by transform, no box) read as off the roadway too — see relation_coverage.isIn_edges.

light_state_attribute.available: A change of `light_state` between adjacent frames, readable with the temporal operators; no extra field is needed.
light_state_attribute.mechanism: carla_sgg/sgg.py:639 writes `light_state = str(actor.state)` on each traffic-light node every frame.
light_state_attribute.data_limit: A change is observable only between two captured frames, so the resolution is one frame — the interval lives at time_base.capture_hz. Amber is a distinct `light_state` value, not an interpolation.

node_coordinates.available: Every actor-like node carries `vertex` and `forward`, lifted by carla/adapter.py as `pos_x`/`pos_y`/`pos_z` and `fwd_x`/`fwd_y`/`fwd_z`. `Core/Decimal.lean` reads them as integer millimetres, so a SQUARED separation is exact integer arithmetic and needs no square root: an exact metric distance is available even though the six proximity bands are all the edges carry. `forward` is an absolute heading on every actor-like node, so two NON-EGO actors' directions of travel can be compared — which the angular relations, drawn from the ego only and relative, cannot express. Where the capture carries `threedbbox`, the node's half-extents along its own axes are lifted as `half_length`/`half_width`/`half_height`, so the gap between two bodies' SURFACES can be bounded from both sides where `pos_*` gives only centre to centre. The ego additionally carries `vel_*` and `acc_*` as components; the scalar `speed` and `accel` are magnitudes and so carry no sign, and projecting the vector onto the heading is what recovers travelling-backwards from moving, and braking from accelerating.
node_coordinates.mechanism: carla_sgg/sgg.py:798 `__add_to_graph` creates every actor-like node with `vertex`, `forward`, `right`, `up`, `vertex_point` and `threedbbox`, and sgg_abstractor.py:241 copies that dict into the RSV node whole. Every code path that adds an actor, a signal, a sign, a landmark or map scenery goes through __add_to_graph, so the coordinates are always there.
node_coordinates.data_limit: Structure nodes — lane, road, junction, offRoad — carry NO attributes at all: sgg_abstractor.py builds them as `Node(name=...)` with the `attr` default (:145, :147, :152, :222), and the class defines `self.attr = {} if attr is None` (:19-23). So they have no position and no separation can be computed to or between them. A separation predicate is false, not unknown, when a node lacks coordinates; pair it with `Pred.hasPosition` when that distinction matters. The band edges are cut on the THREE-dimensional separation (sgg_abstractor.py:265) while `sepSqMilli` drops the vertical component, so on a gradient the two can disagree by one band. A traffic-light node's raw `forward` is a point rather than a direction on one generator path; the adapter repairs it before lifting (see attribute_keys.fwd_x).
node_coordinates.vocabulary: Pred.withinCentimetres / withinMetresExact / beyondCentimetres / hasPosition, alongside the band-based Pred.withinMetres; Pred.hasExtent / surfaceGapAtLeastCentimetres / surfaceGapAtMostCentimetres over the extents; and the vector family Pred.hasHeading / headingAlignedWith / headingOpposedTo / movingForward / movingBackward / deceleratingAtLeast / acceleratingAtLeast

no_note_needed.$comment: Elements of Core/Scene.lean that need no reading note: their meaning is exactly what the enumeration says. Listed explicitly so `doctor` can prove this section covers the whole data model rather than the parts one law corpus happened to need.

$comment: Why a key the generator emits is NOT lifted. The keys themselves are derived — everything carla_sgg writes, minus what carla/adapter.py reads — so this section carries only the reasons, grouped. A key that stops being emitted, or starts being lifted, changes the derived set without anyone editing this file.
A law needing one of these is NOT unsupported. It is blocked on an adapter and vocabulary extension, which the plan must request explicitly.

Every reason must hold for any law: volume, redundancy with a key already lifted, a value that is not a measurement, or a version-conditional branch. Reasons of the form 'no statute refers to this' describe one corpus and do not belong here.

`matches` is a list of regular expressions, not a list of keys. A pattern covers a family — every `landmark_*` geometry field, say — so a key the generator adds later falls into the right group with no edit here, while `doctor` still fails if any emitted-and-unlifted key matches no group.

redundant_with_a_key_already_lifted.carla_type_id: The blueprint id, already lifted as `sem_class`.
redundant_with_a_key_already_lifted.vehicle_light_state: The packed integer whose bits are lifted individually as the light_* booleans.

not_a_usable_value.light_All: An enum mask over `carla.VehicleLightState.names` meaning all lamps, not a lamp. sgg.py:689 writes one boolean per enum member and this is a member.
not_a_usable_value.light_NONE: The complementary mask, meaning no lamps. Same mechanism.

landmark_physical_geometry.why: The shape and pose of a sign, and its authoring label. Nothing can relate the pose to the lanes it governs: lane, road and junction nodes carry no attributes at all (sgg_abstractor.py:19-23 and the attribute-free `Node(name=...)` constructions at :145, :147, :152), so there are no coordinates on the other side of the comparison. `landmark_name` is a free-text label with no defined vocabulary; the legend a sign displays is `landmark_text`, which is lifted. The landmark fields that state governance or identity — `landmark_lane_validities`, `landmark_orientation`, `landmark_is_dynamic`, `landmark_id` — ARE lifted, so this group is exactly the residue of the `landmark_*` family after them.

a_different_abstraction_would_be_needed_.waypoint_detail: Lane width, both lane markings (colour / type / width / lane_change), `waypoint_s`, `is_junction`, `angle` and `curve` exist on the BASE graph's waypoint nodes, but process_to_junction_rsv collapses every waypoint of a lane into one lane node and keeps none of them. Not reachable by extending the adapter.

volume.$comment: Sized from the generator, not from a capture: the count of numbers each key contributes PER NODE PER FRAME, which is fixed by the code that writes it. The generated Lean trace is chunked to stay under Lean's per-definition codegen limit, so what matters is numbers per node per frame rather than any one capture's total.
volume.vertex_point: The same x,y as `vertex`, as a shapely POINT. `vertex` is lifted as pos_x/pos_y/pos_z, so this is a second copy in a form Lean cannot read. `threedbbox`, `right` and `up` used to sit here too; they are now CONSUMED — reduced by carla/adapter.py to the three half-extents, three numbers in place of thirty — and so are on the lifted side of the partition under `half_length`/`half_width`/`half_height`.

conditional_on_the_carla_version.why: Written only inside the `for bbox in actor.get_light_boxes()` branch (sgg.py:585-612), guarded by `except AttributeError` for CARLA builds lacking that method; the fallback (:613-625) writes `carla_id` and `carla_type_id` only, one node per light rather than one per lamp head, with a correct `forward`. Which branch a capture took is readable from the trace: the fallback leaves `carla_parent_id` and its siblings absent. `carla_parent_id` is the one with content — it ties the individual lamp heads of a junction to a parent signal, which is the signal grouping nothing else provides — and it is None whenever the light has no parent actor. Not lifted, so a rule needing it is a vocabulary gap to request.

commanded_control.why: The control a CALLER passed to generate_graph_for_frame, written as `ego_control_<key>` (sgg.py:565-570) beside the applied control `copy_carla_control` reads back from the server for the ego (:562), which IS lifted as throttle/brake/steer/hand_brake/reverse/gear/manual_gear_shift. The commanded and the applied control describe one input at most one tick apart, so the second copy adds no evidence a rule could read differently. Present only on captures whose script passed the argument.

$comment: Settings a CALLER chooses, which no capture is obliged to record. Each entry names the generator parameter(s) it accounts for, says where the value lives, and says what breaks if a capture used a different one — it never restates the value, so there is one place to change it.

Complete over the generator's own signature, not over the settings someone thought of: `parameters` is checked against scripts/diagnostics/sgg_surface.py::parameters(), which reads the keyword arguments of SGG.__initialization, init_to_world, generate_graph_for_frame and process_to_junction_rsv. `run_spec doctor` fails when a parameter exists in the generator and is accounted for nowhere here.

Why they must be FIXED, not merely recorded: frozen Core encodes several of them as constants — Core/Scene.lean::captureHz, ::distanceBands, ::proximityTypes, and the four angular labels Vocab.lean reads. A trace built from a capture made with other settings still type-checks and still grounds, but its keys no longer MEAN what Core assumes: the same band label denotes a different distance, the same frame count a different duration. The rules then evaluate correctly against the wrong world. Nothing in the trace reveals it, and an unparseable or out-of-range value makes both `leMilli` and `geMilli` false, so the error direction is a MISSED violation.
So the four that Core mirrors are refused by carla/adapter.py, and the rest warn. A capture is only comparable with another when both used the same settings.

capture_rate.note: The value lives in Core/Scene.lean::captureHz, and nowhere else. It is `world.settings.fixed_delta_seconds` inverted, chosen by the capture script, and `secondsToFrames` multiplies by it. Frames carry no timestamp, so the rate is unverifiable from the data by construction. Halving or doubling it rescales every duration in every rule: a one-second dwell requirement becomes half a second, and a rolling stop satisfies it.

proximity_band_metres.note: The value lives in Core/Scene.lean::distanceBands. It is `DEFAULT_PROXIMITY_THRESHOLDS`, an overridable parameter of process_to_junction_rsv. The RSV keeps only the band LABEL, not the metres (edge data keys are exactly {'label'}), so the mapping cannot be recovered from a capture. Different thresholds silently redefine what every `Pred.withinMetres N` bound means.

proximity_pair_table.note: The value lives in Core/Scene.lean::proximityTypes. It is `DEFAULT_PROXIMITY_RELATIONS` / `DEFAULT_DIRECTIONAL_RELATIONS`, both overridable. 'ego is always one end' is a property of the default table, not of the generator.

directional_split_degrees.note: `DEFAULT_DIRECTIONAL_THRESHOLDS`, overridable. `Pred.oncoming`'s 'headings differ by more than 90 degrees' is a property of that table.

junction_boundaries.note: init_to_world(parse_junction_boundaries=False). When set, the generator places a `junction_boundary` node at every junction entry through __add_to_graph (sgg.py:360-408), so unlike every other structure element it carries a position and a heading; carla/adapter.py keys its identity on that position, the RSV name being a per-frame counter.

segment_length.note: SGG(segment_length=1.0). Sets lane-node granularity, and also appears in the `controls`-edge test (`get_distance(...) < self.segment_length * 0.5`), so every governance edge carries a tolerance derived from it. Any rule reading `controls` or `mayAffect` inherits that tolerance.

excluded_actors.note: generate_graph_for_frame(exclude_ids=None). Actors listed here are dropped from the frame entirely. The ego is always appended to it, which is WHY the ego carries no light_* attributes — see attribute_keys. A caller passing more ids removes those actors from the graph with no trace in the capture, so a rule about them would ground zero times for a reason nothing records.

which_actor_is_the_ego.note: SGG(ego_id=None). Selects which CARLA actor becomes the `ego` node, and the ego node is privileged throughout: it is the only node carrying the dynamics channels (sgg.py:562-563), the only one excluded from every frame's actor list, and one end of every proximity and angular edge. Pointing it at a different vehicle does not rename a node — it changes which vehicle every ego-scoped predicate is about, and so which vehicle any verdict describes.

ego_control_source.note: generate_graph_for_frame(ego_control=None). The seven control channels a rule reads (throttle, brake, steer, hand_brake, reverse, gear, manual_gear_shift) come from `copy_carla_control(ego.get_control(), ...)` at sgg.py:562 and are written whatever this argument is. When a caller also passes a control, :565-570 writes it beside them as `ego_control_<key>` — a second copy, not lifted (see available_not_exposed.commanded_control).

base_graph_construction.note: SGG(init=True, frame_buffer=10) and generate_graph_for_frame(perform_init=False). `init` builds the whole base graph at construction; `perform_init` does it lazily on the first frame instead. Either way the road structure is fixed before frame 0 — see when_they_are_fixed. `frame_buffer` sizes the generator's internal snapshot history and changes no node, edge or attribute.

capture_preconditions.how_to_fix: Record the generator/simulator parameters alongside each capture and have carla/adapter.py hard-fail on disagreement with what Core assumes. Until then these are assumptions, not facts, and must be presented as such to anyone planning against them.
capture_preconditions.when_they_are_fixed: All SGG parameters are INIT-ONLY. `SGG.__initialization` calls `init_to_world()` when `init=True` (the default), which builds the whole base graph — road structure, lane nodes, lane bounding boxes, waypoint sampling — from these values in one pass. Every setter then calls `_check_init()`, which raises `ValueError: Cannot initialize or alter parameters after initialization. You must use a separate SGG object per map and configuration`. So they cannot drift mid-capture: they are per-capture constants decided before frame 0. `SGG.__new__` is a singleton that DELETES and recreates the instance when called with arguments, so constructing SGG again with different values rebuilds the base graph — which is the only way to change them, and it changes every frame that follows. Nothing in a capture records which values were used; carla_scene_graphs/src/carlaspec/runner.py writes them into simulation.json → generator, and carla/adapter.py refuses a capture whose recorded values contradict what Core assumes.

no_effect_on_this_abstraction.$comment: Parameters that look as though they should matter and do not. Each was traced through the generator source to every use site, and reaches no node, edge or attribute of this abstraction. Recorded so they are not mistaken for silent hazards.
no_effect_on_this_abstraction.closeness_inflation: SGG(closeness_inflation=0.25). Feeds `hashable_location(vert, waypoint_precision, inflation)`, which buckets waypoint vertices onto a grid of `segment_length / inflation` = 4 m, building `closeness_map`. That map is stored on the base graph (sgg.py:346) and then DELETED from every frame subgraph (sgg.py:725) without ever being read. No edge, node or attribute depends on it.
no_effect_on_this_abstraction.angular_precision: SGG(angular_precision=[1, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10]). Buckets each waypoint's turn angle into the node attributes `angle` and `curve`. Only `process_to_abstract()` reads `curve` (sgg_abstractor.py:58), and this pipeline consumes `process_to_junction_rsv`, which reads neither — waypoint runs are collapsed into one lane node carrying only a name.
no_effect_on_this_abstraction.frame_buffer: SGG(frame_buffer=10). Sizes two LRU caches of recent frames. Affects memory and recomputation, not output.
